title: 해외 여행
intro: 해외 여행은 '좋아하는 나라·도시 묘사 → 여행 준비 루틴 → 여행 중 문제·돌발 상황 경험 → 첫 해외여행과 지금 비교' 순서로 자주 출제됩니다. 작년 여름 가족과 간 일본 오사카(유니버설 스튜디오, 먹자골목)와 신입 때 첫 해외였던 미국 샌프란시스코 출장 두 가지 이야기만 준비하면 묘사·경험·비교 질문을 모두 커버할 수 있습니다. 문제 경험은 '오사카 지하철에서 아들이 가방을 두고 내린 일'로 고정하세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Sure, I'd love to talk about ~) → 어디를 언제 누구와 갔는지 기본 정보 → 한 일·먹은 음식·아이들 반응 세부 → 좋았던 이유·느낌 → 마무리 문장(So yeah, that's why ~)
도시는 오사카(작년 여름, 가족 넷, 유니버설 스튜디오, 도톤보리 타코야키)로 고정하고, 비교 질문에서만 20년 전 샌프란시스코 출장을 꺼내세요.
문제 경험은 '무슨 일이 생겼다 → 당황했다 → 역무실에 가서 해결 → 그 뒤로 생긴 습관' 4단계로 말하면 시간 순서가 분명해져요.
비교 질문은 '신입 때는 스마트폰도 없이 종이 지도와 출력한 일정표 → 지금은 앱으로 지도·번역·예약'처럼 기술 변화를 개발자다운 시선으로 말하세요.

expressions.en: Sure, I'd love to talk about my trip to Osaka.
expressions.ko: 네, 제 오사카 여행에 대해 말해 볼게요.
expressions.note: 해외 여행 질문의 시작 문장으로 그대로 사용

expressions.en: I went to Japan with my family last summer.
The flight took about an hour and a half.
The food was cheap and delicious.
I booked the flights and the hotel online.
I always pack our passports first.
I didn't know what to do.
expressions.note: 문제 경험에서 당황한 순간을 말할 때

expressions.en: We waited in line for over an hour.
expressions.note: wait in line: 줄 서서 기다리다

expressions.en: The staff were really kind and helpful.
expressions.ko: 직원들이 정말 친절하고 도움이 많이 됐어요.

expressions.en: It was my first time going abroad.
Everything is so much easier with a smartphone.
expressions.ko: 스마트폰이 있으니 모든 게 훨씬 쉬워요.

expressions.en: My heart sank when I realized the bag was gone.
expressions.ko: 가방이 없어진 걸 알았을 때 가슴이 철렁했어요.
expressions.note: my heart sank: 철렁하다, 덜컥 겁이 나다

expressions.en: It was a huge weight off my shoulders.
expressions.note: 걱정이 해결됐을 때 쓰는 관용 표현

expressions.en: So yeah, that's why I love traveling abroad with my family.
expressions.ko: 그래서 제가 가족과 해외여행 가는 걸 정말 좋아해요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like to travel abroad. Tell me about a country or city you have visited and really liked. What was it like, and what did you enjoy doing there?
questions.ko: 설문에서 해외여행을 좋아한다고 하셨습니다. 가 본 나라나 도시 중 정말 좋았던 곳에 대해 말해 주세요. 어땠고, 거기서 무엇을 즐겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·누구와·어디(작년 여름, 가족, 오사카) → 한 일(유니버설 스튜디오, 도톤보리 먹거리) → 좋았던 이유 → 'So yeah, that's why ~' 마무리
과거에 다녀온 곳이므로 묘사는 과거 시제, 도시의 특징(It's famous for ~)은 현재 시제로 섞어 쓰세요.
'회사 일을 잊고 가족과 시간을 보냈다'는 직장인 감정 포인트를 이유로 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Sure, I'd love to talk about my trip to Osaka. I went to Japan with my family last summer. The flight took about an hour and a half from Incheon. Osaka is a big and lively city. We went to Universal Studios, and my kids loved it. We also walked around Dotonbori and ate takoyaki. The food was cheap and delicious. The people were really kind, too. I forgot all about work for a few days. So yeah, that's why I really liked Osaka.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about my trip to Osaka. One of my favorite things to do is traveling abroad with my family, and Osaka was our best trip so far. We went there last summer for four days. The flight from Incheon only took about an hour and a half, so it was easy with the kids. Osaka is a big city, but it's not too crowded or stressful. It has a fun and lively atmosphere that makes me feel like a kid again. On the second day, we spent the whole day at Universal Studios. My son loved the roller coasters, and my daughter loved the Minions. At night, we walked around Dotonbori and ate takoyaki and ramen. Spending time with my family helps me forget about work. So yeah, that's why I really liked Osaka.
answers.AL: Oh, a city I really liked? Let me think. I'd have to say Osaka, for sure. One of my favorite things to do is traveling abroad with my family, and our trip to Osaka last summer was the best one so far. It's only about an hour and a half from Incheon, so it's perfect for a short family trip. What I liked most about Osaka is the energy. The streets are full of bright signs and food stalls, and people are really friendly. It has a fun and lively atmosphere that makes me feel like a kid again. The highlight was definitely Universal Studios. We got there right when it opened and still waited in line for over an hour for some rides, but nobody complained. My son went on the biggest roller coaster three times, and my daughter took about a hundred pictures with the Minions. In the evenings, we wandered around Dotonbori, grabbing takoyaki and bowls of ramen. Honestly, I gained a few kilos. At home, I'm always busy with meetings and projects, so I don't get much time with the kids. Spending time with my family helps me forget about work. So yeah, that's why Osaka is one of my favorite cities.

questions.en: What do you usually do to prepare for a trip abroad? Tell me about all the steps you take, from booking the trip to packing your bags.
questions.ko: 해외여행을 가기 전에 보통 어떤 준비를 하나요? 예약부터 짐 싸기까지 거치는 모든 단계를 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 예약(항공권·호텔) → 일정 짜기(아이들과 함께) → 서류·환전·유심 → 짐 싸기 → 'Yeah, that's how ~' 마무리
First, Then, After that, Finally 같은 순서 표현으로 단계를 분명히 나누세요.
'개발자라 체크리스트를 만든다', '여권 4개를 한 파우치에 넣는다'처럼 나만의 습관을 하나 넣으면 IH 이상으로 들려요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about how I prepare for a trip abroad. I usually travel with my family, so I plan early. First, I book the flights and the hotel online. Then, I make a simple plan with my kids. After that, I check our passports. I also get some yen or dollars and buy a SIM card for my phone. The night before, we pack our bags together. I always pack our passports first. Yeah, that's how I get ready for a trip abroad.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about how I prepare for a trip abroad. Traveling with a family of four takes a lot of planning, so I usually start about three months before. First, I book the flights and the hotel. Then, I make a simple plan with my kids. My son picks one activity, and my daughter picks one, so everyone is happy. After that, I check our passports and make sure they aren't expiring soon. A week before we leave, I exchange some money and buy a data SIM card online. The night before, we pack together. I put all four passports in one small pouch, and I keep it in my bag the whole trip. On the day, we get to the airport about three hours early. So yeah, that's pretty much how I prepare for a trip abroad.
answers.AL: Oh, getting ready for a trip abroad? Let me think. Honestly, with two kids, it's almost like running a small project at work. I usually start about three months before, because flights get really expensive if you wait. First, I book the flights and the hotel. Then, I make a simple plan with my kids. We sit down together, and each of them gets to choose one thing they really want to do. Last year in Osaka, my son chose Universal Studios, and my daughter chose a big cat cafe. After that, I go through all the boring stuff. I check that our passports aren't expiring, book travel insurance, and buy a data SIM card online. I'm a developer, so of course I make a checklist on my phone and check things off one by one. A week before, I exchange a bit of cash, just in case. The night before we leave, the whole family packs together. I put all four passports in one small pouch and never let it out of my sight. On the day, we get to the airport three hours early, because I hate rushing. So yeah, that's pretty much how I get ready for a trip abroad.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem or an unexpected situation while traveling abroad? Tell me about that experience in detail. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
questions.ko: 해외여행 중에 문제나 예상치 못한 상황을 겪은 적이 있나요? 그 경험을 자세히 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 어떻게 해결했나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·어디서(작년 여름 오사카 지하철) → 무슨 일(아들이 가방을 두고 내림) → 어떻게 해결(역무실, 다음 역에서 찾음) → 배운 점 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
Something unexpected happened when ~ / I didn't know what to do, so I ~ / Luckily, ~ 세 문장이 문제 경험의 뼈대예요.
끝에 'Since then, I always make sure to ~'로 교훈을 붙이면 자연스럽게 마무리돼요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem while traveling? Let me think. Last summer, I went to Osaka with my family. Something unexpected happened when we were taking the subway. My son left his backpack on the train. His wallet and phone were in it. I didn't know what to do, so I went to the station office. The staff called the next station. Luckily, they found the bag, and we got it back an hour later. Since then, I always make sure to check our seats before we get off. Yeah, that's my story.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. Last summer, my family and I went to Osaka for four days. Something unexpected happened when we were taking the subway back to our hotel. Everyone was really tired after a long day at Universal Studios. When we got off the train, my son suddenly shouted, 'My backpack!' He left it on the seat, and his phone and wallet were inside. The train was already gone. I didn't know what to do, so I went to the station office. My Japanese is terrible, so I used a translation app on my phone. The staff were really kind. They called the next station, and luckily, someone found the bag. We took the next train and picked it up. Nothing was missing. Since then, I always make sure to check our seats before we get off. Yeah, that's my story.
answers.AL: Oh, an unexpected situation? Actually, yes, I have a pretty good one. Last summer, my family and I went to Osaka. Something unexpected happened when we were taking the subway back to our hotel. We had just spent the whole day at Universal Studios, so all four of us were completely exhausted. We got off at our stop, and about ten seconds later, my son shouted, 'My backpack!' He'd left it on the seat, with his phone, his wallet, and all the souvenirs he'd bought. My heart sank when I realized the train was already gone. I didn't know what to do, so I went to the station office. My Japanese is pretty much limited to 'thank you,' so I typed everything into a translation app and showed the staff my phone. They were incredibly calm and kind. One staff member called the next station, and within a few minutes, they found the bag. We hopped on the next train, and there it was, waiting for us at the counter. Nothing was missing. It was a huge weight off my shoulders. It turned out to be a great lesson, though. Since then, I always make sure to check our seats before we get off. Yeah, that's my story.

questions.en: How is the way you travel abroad now different from the first time you traveled overseas? Or, how does traveling abroad compare to traveling within Korea?
questions.ko: 지금의 해외여행 방식은 처음 해외에 나갔을 때와 어떻게 다른가요? 또는 해외여행은 국내 여행과 비교해 어떤가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 첫 해외(20년 전 신입 때 샌프란시스코 출장, 스마트폰 없음) → 지금(가족 여행, 앱으로 지도·번역·예약) → 가장 큰 차이와 이유 → 'Yeah, that's how ~' 마무리
Compared to ~, ~ is much ~ 패턴으로 핵심 차이를 한 문장에 정리하세요.
'출력한 지도와 일정표 → 스마트폰 앱'처럼 기술 변화를 말하면 개발자 페르소나와 잘 어울려요.

answers.IM3: Oh, how my travel has changed? Let me think. My first trip abroad was about twenty years ago. I went to San Francisco on a business trip. I was a new employee, and I was really nervous. I didn't have a smartphone, so I used paper maps. Now I travel with my family. I use apps for maps, booking, and translation. Compared to my first trip, traveling abroad now is much easier. Yeah, that's how my trips abroad have changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. My first trip abroad was about twenty years ago, when I was a new developer. My company sent me to San Francisco on a business trip with two seniors. I was so nervous because my English wasn't very good. Back then, I didn't have a smartphone, so I printed out maps and the hotel address before I left. I even got lost once on the way to a meeting. Now everything is different. I travel for fun with my family, and I do everything on my phone. I book flights with an app, use maps to find restaurants, and use a translation app when I need it. Compared to my first trip, traveling abroad now is much easier. The biggest difference is technology. Yeah, that's how my trips abroad have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a fun one. Let me think. My first trip abroad was about twenty years ago, right after I joined my company. They sent me to San Francisco on a business trip with two senior developers. I was excited, but honestly, I was terrified. My English was pretty basic, and I didn't have a smartphone. I printed out maps, the hotel address, and even the directions to the office, and I carried them everywhere in a folder. One morning, I took the wrong bus and showed up twenty minutes late to a meeting. I still remember how red my face was. Fast forward to now, and it's a completely different world. These days, I travel with my family, mostly for fun, and my phone does almost everything. I book flights on an app, find restaurants with a map, and if I get stuck, I just open a translation app. Last summer in Osaka, I barely needed any Japanese at all. Compared to my first trip, traveling abroad now is much easier and much less stressful. I think this change is mostly because of smartphones. Yeah, that's how my trips abroad have changed over the years.

pronunciation.tip: 뒤 '브로-드'에 강세. 앞 a는 '어'로 약하게 흘려요.
앞 '패'에 강세를 주고 '패스포-트'. 끝 t는 살짝만 끊어요.
미국식은 '스케줄', 영국식은 '셰듈'. 한 가지로 일관되게 쓰세요.

patterns.ko: 제가 가장 좋아하는 일 중 하나는 가족과 해외여행을 가는 거예요.

patterns.en: It has a fun and lively atmosphere that makes me feel like a kid again.
patterns.ko: 다시 아이가 된 기분이 들게 하는 즐겁고 활기찬 분위기가 있어요.

patterns.en: Spending time with my family helps me forget about work.
patterns.ko: 가족과 시간을 보내면 일을 잊는 데 도움이 돼요.

patterns.en: First, I book the flights and the hotel. Then, I make a simple plan with my kids.
patterns.ko: 먼저 항공권과 호텔을 예약해요. 그다음 아이들과 간단한 일정을 짜요.

patterns.en: Something unexpected happened when we were taking the subway.
patterns.ko: 지하철을 타고 가던 중에 예상치 못한 일이 생겼어요.

patterns.en: I didn't know what to do, so I went to the station office.
patterns.ko: 어떻게 해야 할지 몰라서 역무실로 갔어요.

patterns.en: Since then, I always make sure to check our seats before we get off.
patterns.ko: 그 뒤로 저는 내리기 전에 항상 자리를 꼭 확인해요.

patterns.en: Compared to my first trip, traveling abroad now is much easier.
patterns.ko: 첫 여행에 비해 지금은 해외여행이 훨씬 쉬워요.
